steps.prompt: Before the check: which number theory tool do you reach for fastest now, and which one do you still have to stop and think about?

cards.title: Divisibility, primes, GCD & LCM: quick review
cards.body: Tests: $4$ and $8$ use the last two or three digits, $3$ and $9$ the digit sum, $11$ the alternating sum. Combine tests whose numbers share no factor ($12 = 3 \times 4$). Factor into primes; test primes only up to $\sqrt{n}$. GCD: smaller powers; LCM: larger powers; $\gcd \times \text{lcm} = ab$.

cards.title: Divisors & factorials: quick review
cards.body: $p^a q^b$ has $(a + 1)(b + 1)$ divisors; only squares have an odd number. Zeros of $n!$: $\left\lfloor \frac{n}{5} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{n}{25} \right\rfloor + \cdots$, and the same count with any prime $p$ gives its power in $n!$.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First a short warm-up. Then the check: $8$ AMC-style problems with choices, easiest first, no hints. You need all $8$ right (100%) to pass. If you miss one, you'll see the solutions and which skills to review, and the next try gives you new problems.

prompts: Which habit from this unit will you use first on your next test?
Which skill will you keep practising in the daily review?
